cardiff.seoTitle: Schools in Cardiff Catchment 2026 — Postcode Map & List
cardiff.seoDescription: Cardiff area catchment finder: 124 schools, every catchment boundary mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year — free.
paragraphs: Cardiff's 124 schools span every phase from nursery through to sixth form, making it the largest concentration of state schools in Wales. Admissions are coordinated by Cardiff Council, which publishes catchment boundaries and oversubscription criteria each September for the following academic year.

Because Cardiff is a bilingual city, many schools offer Welsh-medium education alongside English-medium provision — and catchment areas for Welsh-medium schools are typically wider to reflect lower pupil density. Check each school's admissions policy carefully, as Welsh-medium and English-medium catchments rarely overlap.

worthing.seoTitle: Worthing School Catchment Map 2026 — 24 Primaries by Postcode
worthing.seoDescription: Worthing area catchment finder: 24 primary + 6 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. West Sussex 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Worthing's 38 schools sit within West Sussex County Council's admissions remit, with catchment boundaries drawn for each of its 24 primary schools based on measured distances from the school gate. Oversubscription at popular primaries such as those near the seafront and in Goring-by-Sea can push offers beyond 1 mile in quieter years, but fell inside 0.8 miles during the 2024 round — so address matters here.

The town's 6 secondary schools include both comprehensive and faith options, and several have their own supplementary information forms for faith criteria. West Sussex publishes its co-ordinated secondary offer on National Offer Day (1 March) and its primary offer on 16 April — use the catchment.school postcode tool to check each school's last-offered distance before applying.

ely.seoDescription: Ely area catchment finder: 19 primary + 4 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Cambridgeshire 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.

barnet.seoTitle: Barnet School Catchment Map 2026 — 14 Primaries by Postcode
barnet.seoDescription: Barnet area catchment finder: 14 primary + 5 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered — free.
paragraphs: Barnet has 25 schools in this area including 14 primaries and 5 secondaries, with Barnet Council co-ordinating admissions for community schools. Four academies and five faith schools apply their own criteria, which typically give priority to children attending specified feeder primaries or of the relevant faith denomination.

Distance tiebreakers at Barnet community secondaries are measured from home address to the nearest school entrance. With house prices among the highest in North London, competition for places at the most sought-after schools in this part of the borough is intense, and some catchments cover less than 0.5 km.

rochdale.seoTitle: Rochdale School Catchment Map 2026 — 41 Primaries by Postcode
rochdale.seoDescription: Rochdale area catchment finder: 41 primary + 8 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Greater Manchester 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Rochdale has 64 schools including 41 primaries and 8 secondaries, spread across towns such as Heywood, Middleton and Littleborough. Rochdale Council co-ordinates admissions for community schools, but 26 academies and 19 faith schools (primarily Church of England and Roman Catholic) apply their own criteria.

Oversubscription at popular Rochdale primaries is often settled by straight-line distance, though a number of Roman Catholic schools draw pupils from a much wider parish catchment. The council publishes 'last distance offered' data in its annual admissions booklet, usually released in October.

bourne.seoTitle: Bourne School Catchment Map 2026 — 6 Primaries by Postcode
bourne.seoDescription: Bourne area catchment finder: 6 primary + 2 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Lincolnshire 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Bourne has 10 schools including 6 primaries and 2 secondaries in Lincolnshire. Nine of the ten schools operate as academies, meaning each sets its own admissions criteria — though in practice most follow the LA's standard distance-based tiebreaker for oversubscription.

Bourne Grammar School is partially selective and requires the Lincolnshire 11+ transfer test, so parents of children approaching Year 6 should register for the test by the deadline in June. For non-selective secondary places, Bourne Community College allocates via Lincolnshire's co-ordinated scheme.

abingdon.seoTitle: Abingdon School Catchment Map 2026 — 21 Primaries by Postcode
abingdon.seoDescription: Abingdon area catchment finder: 21 primary + 3 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Oxfordshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered — free.
paragraphs: Abingdon-on-Thames has 32 schools within Oxfordshire County Council's admissions area — 21 primaries and 3 secondaries, with a strong Church of England sector that operates supplementary faith criteria. The town's growth along the A34 corridor has increased pressure on places in the newer residential areas south of the town centre.

The three secondary schools — Larkmead, John Mason and Fitzharrys — are all comprehensive 11–18 schools and serve distinct parts of the town. Oxfordshire's co-ordinated scheme requires secondary preferences by October and primary preferences by January; families in the Vale of White Horse area closest to Didcot should also compare schools in that town.

sunbury-on-thames.seoTitle: Sunbury-on-Thames School Catchment Map 2026 — 6 Primaries by Postcode
sunbury-on-thames.seoDescription: Sunbury-on-Thames catchment finder: 6 primary + 3 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Surrey 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Sunbury-on-Thames sits within Surrey County Council's admissions area, with 11 schools covering both the original town centre and the newer Sunbury Cross and Lower Sunbury districts. Surrey uses straight-line distance as the final tiebreaker at all community primaries, and in Sunbury — where primary rolls are capped and new capacity has not kept pace with housing growth — last-offered distances at the most popular schools have historically been under 0.6 miles.

Three secondary schools primarily serve the area: Sunbury Manor, Halliford and — for families on the Thames-side stretch — Matthew Arnold in Staines. All are comprehensive. Surrey co-ordinates secondary offers through its online application system, with the deadline for secondary preferences in October and primary preferences in November.

sutton-coldfield.seoTitle: Sutton Coldfield School Catchment Map 2026 — 31 Primaries by Postcode
sutton-coldfield.seoDescription: Sutton Coldfield area catchment finder: 31 primary + 8 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Birmingham 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Sutton Coldfield's 42 schools are administered by Birmingham City Council, whose Primary and Secondary Determined Admission Arrangements set out the oversubscription criteria for each school. The town's 31 primaries span the full spectrum from heavily oversubscribed Church of England schools in the town centre to newer community schools in developments along Mere Green Road and New Hall, where distances offered can be considerably longer.

Eight secondary schools serve the area, including Plantsbrook, Bishop Vesey's Grammar (selective — 11-plus required) and Sutton Coldfield Grammar School for Girls (also selective). Families in the SK4–B73–B76 postcode corridor should apply to Birmingham's co-ordinated scheme in October for secondary places and in January for primary — late applications drop to a lower priority tier.

sittingbourne.seoDescription: Sittingbourne area catchment finder: 26 primary + 5 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Kent 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered — free.

welwyn-garden-city.seoDescription: Welwyn Garden City catchment finder: 16 primary + 3 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Hertfordshire 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.

barrow-in-furness.seoTitle: Barrow-in-Furness School Catchment Map 2026 — 24 Primaries by Postcode
barrow-in-furness.seoDescription: Barrow-in-Furness catchment finder: 24 primary + 3 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Westmorland and Furness 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Barrow-in-Furness has 32 schools administered by Westmorland and Furness Council (formed in April 2023 from the merger of Barrow, Eden and South Lakeland districts). The town's 24 primaries serve distinct residential zones — Walney Island, Ormsgill, Hawcoat and the town centre — and many are undersubscribed, meaning most applicants living reasonably close receive a place at their preferred school.

Three secondary schools dominate the secondary sector: Barrow Sixth Form College feeds from Thorncliffe and Furness Academy, while St Bernard's Catholic High School draws from across the peninsula on faith criteria. Westmorland and Furness publishes its co-ordinated scheme annually; families are advised to name three preferences in October to maximise choice.

flintshire.seoTitle: Schools in Flintshire Catchment 2026 — Postcode Map & List
flintshire.seoDescription: Flintshire area catchment finder: 55 schools, every catchment boundary mapped to your postcode. 2026 Welsh admissions criteria, Estyn ratings and distance offered last year — free.

ashbourne.seoTitle: Ashbourne School Catchment Map 2026 — 21 Primaries by Postcode
ashbourne.seoDescription: Ashbourne area catchment finder: 21 primary + 1 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Derbyshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered — free.
paragraphs: Ashbourne is a Derbyshire market town with 22 schools, the vast majority of which are rural primaries in the surrounding villages of the Dove Valley and Ecclesbourne catchment. Derbyshire County Council is the admissions authority for most community schools, while several Church of England primaries follow their own voluntary-aided criteria.

Thomas Alleyne's High School is the sole secondary in the town and draws from a wide rural hinterland — including pupils from Staffordshire parishes just across the county border. Parental preference is strong here: the school is typically oversubscribed by local families, so checking the published last-offered distance in the school's admissions policy is important for families moving to the area.

barton-upon-humber.seoTitle: Barton-upon-Humber School Catchment Map 2026 — 4 Primaries by Postcode
barton-upon-humber.seoDescription: Barton-upon-Humber catchment finder: 4 primary + 1 secondary school mapped to your postcode. North Lincolnshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Barton-upon-Humber is a small North Lincolnshire market town with 6 schools — 4 primaries and 1 secondary — all administered by North Lincolnshire Council. The town sits on the southern bank of the Humber, connected to Hull by the Humber Bridge, and its schools reflect a settled community with relatively stable rolls.

Baysgarth School is the main secondary, serving Barton and the surrounding villages. It is non-selective and typically admits all applicants from its defined catchment area. North Lincolnshire co-ordinates its admissions through its published scheme; applications open in September for the following September's intake.

blaydon-on-tyne.seoTitle: Blaydon-on-Tyne School Catchment Map 2026 — 5 Primaries by Postcode
blaydon-on-tyne.seoDescription: Blaydon-on-Tyne catchment finder: 5 primary + 1 secondary school mapped to your postcode. Gateshead 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Blaydon-on-Tyne has 6 schools — 5 primaries and 1 secondary — with catchment boundaries set by Gateshead Council. Three schools hold faith designations (Roman Catholic) and three operate as academies, so it is worth reading each school's individual admissions policy alongside the council's co-ordinated scheme.

Catchment areas in Blaydon are relatively stable year-on-year, as this is a less densely populated part of Gateshead. However, the Roman Catholic secondary draws pupils from a significantly wider area than the community alternatives, and siblings are always given priority after children with EHC plans.

alresford.seoTitle: Alresford School Catchment Map 2026 — 4 Primaries by Postcode
alresford.seoDescription: Alresford area catchment finder: 4 primary + 1 secondary school mapped to your postcode. Hampshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered — free.
paragraphs: Alresford (also known as New Alresford) is a small Hampshire market town with 6 schools — 4 primaries and Perins Multi-Academy Trust secondary. Hampshire County Council co-ordinates admissions for most community schools, and the town's rural location means the secondary catchment extends across a wide swathe of the Mid-Hants watercress-growing valley.

Perins School is the sole secondary and is consistently well-regarded; it draws pupils from Alresford, Alton, Bishop's Sutton and the surrounding villages. Hampshire's application portal opens in September for secondary preferences (deadline October) and in November for primary preferences (deadline January).

beckenham.seoTitle: Beckenham School Catchment Map 2026 — 11 Primaries by Postcode
beckenham.seoDescription: Beckenham area catchment finder: 11 primary + 5 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Bromley 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Beckenham's 18 schools are administered by the London Borough of Bromley, one of the few London boroughs to retain a selective secondary tier alongside comprehensive schools. Catchment areas for Bromley's community primaries use straight-line distance from home to school, measured by the council's GIS system — in competitive zones near Eden Park and Clock House, last-offered distances at popular primaries can fall below 0.4 miles.

Secondary choices include Langley Park Schools for Boys and Girls, which draw from a wide Bromley catchment, and the partially-selective St Joseph's Academy. Bromley coordinates its secondary offer through the Pan-London Admissions Scheme, with preferences submitted via the council's eAdmissions portal by the October deadline.

norwich.seoTitle: Norwich School Catchment Map 2026 — 142 Primaries by Postcode
norwich.seoDescription: Norwich area catchment finder: 142 primary + 22 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Norfolk 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Norwich is Norfolk's county city and one of the most complex admissions landscapes in the East of England, with 192 schools spanning 142 primaries and 22 secondaries across the city and its immediate fringe. Norfolk County Council is the admissions authority for most community schools, but Norwich has a high proportion of academy and church schools that set their own criteria — checking each school's individual policy is essential.

The secondary sector includes three remaining upper schools operating a middle-school system in parts of Norfolk, alongside standard 11–16 and 11–18 comprehensives. Open-access sixth forms and faith schools add further complexity. Norfolk's co-ordinated scheme requires preferences to be submitted by the October secondary deadline and January primary deadline; the council publishes annual data on last-offered distances for each Norwich school.

loughborough.seoDescription: Loughborough catchment finder: 55 Leicestershire schools — 38 primary + 8 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered — free.

eastleigh.seoTitle: Eastleigh School Catchment Areas 2026 — 22 Primary & 4 Secondary | Hampshire
eastleigh.seoDescription: Eastleigh catchment finder: 30 Hampshire schools — 22 primary + 4 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered — free.
paragraphs: Eastleigh has 30 schools — 22 primaries and 4 secondaries — with catchment boundaries set by Hampshire County Council. The town's rapid residential growth means that catchment boundaries at several popular primaries have contracted in recent years as more families compete for places.

Hampshire uses a straight-line distance tiebreaker at community schools after siblings, looked-after children and special-needs allocations. For secondary schools, check whether your postcode falls within the published catchment area before the October deadline, as out-of-catchment applicants are rarely successful at the most popular schools.

colchester.seoTitle: Colchester School Catchment Areas 2026 — 73 Primary & 15 Secondary | Essex
colchester.seoDescription: Colchester catchment finder: 103 Essex schools — 73 primary + 15 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year — free.
paragraphs: Colchester is Essex's largest town and has 103 schools including 73 primaries and 15 secondaries. Essex County Council co-ordinates admissions, but 44 academies and 29 faith schools (Church of England, Roman Catholic and Christian) each publish their own oversubscription criteria alongside the LA's annual admissions booklet.

Demand is particularly acute for secondary places in the Lexden and Stanway areas, where popular schools routinely fill on distance within a mile or less. Colchester's rapid housing development has pushed several primary catchments below 500 metres at their tightest point, so re-checking boundaries annually is essential.

chorley.seoTitle: Chorley School Catchment Areas 2026 — 40 Primary & 5 Secondary | Lancashire
chorley.seoDescription: Chorley catchment finder: 54 Lancashire schools — 40 primary + 5 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered — free.
paragraphs: Chorley is a large Lancashire town with 54 schools — 40 primaries and 5 secondaries — making it one of the busiest admissions zones in the county. Lancashire County Council co-ordinates all maintained school admissions in Chorley, with catchment areas for community primaries drawn on historical boundaries that do not always align with current residential development patterns.

The town's secondary sector includes Southlands High School, Albany Academy and Parklands High School, which together serve most of Chorley's residential zones. Lancashire operates a three-school preference system for secondary admissions, with the deadline in October; primary applications close in mid-January. Oversubscription is most acute at Church of England primaries in the older village areas.

clitheroe.seoTitle: Clitheroe School Catchment Areas 2026 — Grammar & Comprehensive Guide
clitheroe.seoDescription: Clitheroe catchment finder: 23 Lancashire schools including Clitheroe Royal Grammar — 16 primary + 3 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria and Ofsted ratings — free.
paragraphs: Clitheroe has 23 schools including 16 primaries and 3 secondaries in Lancashire's Ribble Valley. Fourteen of those schools carry a faith designation — predominantly Church of England — reflecting the area's strong historic ties to Anglican and United Reformed Church congregations.

Clitheroe Royal Grammar School is a selective grammar, so Year 6 parents must sit Lancashire's 11+ test to be considered. For non-selective secondary places, Lancashire County Council co-ordinates admissions and applies a distance-from-school-gate tiebreaker at oversubscribed community secondaries.

eastbourne.seoTitle: Eastbourne School Catchment Areas 2026 — 19 Primary & 5 Secondary | East Sussex
eastbourne.seoDescription: Eastbourne catchment finder: 35 East Sussex schools — 19 primary + 5 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered — free.
paragraphs: Eastbourne has 35 schools including 19 primaries and 5 secondaries, administered by East Sussex County Council. The town has a high proportion of academies (22 out of 35) which each set their own admissions policies independently of the local authority.

For primary places in Eastbourne, the main oversubscription tiebreaker at community schools is straight-line distance after special-needs and looked-after children have been allocated. Secondary applicants should note that all five main secondaries are academies or academy trusts, so parents need to read each school's prospectus individually to understand catchment or feeder-school criteria.

burnley.seoTitle: Burnley School Catchment Areas 2026 — 34 Primary & 5 Secondary | Lancashire
burnley.seoDescription: Burnley catchment finder: 61 Lancashire schools — 34 primary + 5 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year — free.
paragraphs: Burnley has 61 schools including 34 primaries and 5 secondaries administered by Lancashire County Council. With 19 faith schools across Church of England and Roman Catholic denominations, Burnley has one of the higher proportions of religiously-designated schools among Lancashire's market towns.

At oversubscribed Burnley community schools, Lancashire uses distance measured along the nearest available walking route rather than straight-line distance — a distinction that can affect who falls just inside or outside a catchment. Secondary places at the town's grammar-stream schools are allocated nationally through Lancashire's grammar co-ordination process.

bridlington.seoTitle: Bridlington School Catchment Areas 2026 — 11 Primary & 2 Secondary Schools
bridlington.seoDescription: Bridlington catchment finder: 14 East Riding of Yorkshire schools — 11 primary + 2 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered — free.

dukinfield.seoTitle: Dukinfield School Catchment Areas 2026 — Tameside Schools Postcode Map
dukinfield.seoDescription: Dukinfield catchment finder: 12 Tameside schools — 6 primary + 2 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered — free.

paragraphs: Kenilworth has 10 schools including 7 primaries and 1 secondary, with catchment boundaries administered by Warwickshire County Council. Three schools operate as Church of England or Roman Catholic faith schools with their own admissions criteria that sit alongside the council's published distance-based policy.

For secondary admissions in Kenilworth, the main oversubscription criterion at community schools is straight-line distance from home to school gate. Parents often find that catchments shift year-on-year depending on application volumes, so checking the previous three years' 'last distance offered' figures is strongly recommended.

Enfield has 50 schools — 32 primaries, 10 secondaries and 8 all-through or special schools. Enfield Council administers community school catchments, while the borough's 16 academies and 12 faith schools (Church of England and Roman Catholic) set their own oversubscription criteria.

Secondary catchment boundaries in Enfield are among the tightest in North London, particularly for schools close to the A10 corridor. Distance to the school gate is the main tiebreaker at community schools; siblings already on roll take priority in round one.

Godalming has 24 schools including 13 primaries and 2 secondaries — all falling under Surrey County Council admissions co-ordination. Of those, 10 are academies or free schools and 10 have a faith designation, making Godalming one of the more complex admissions landscapes in Surrey.

The two main secondary schools in Godalming are Rodborough and Broadwater, both of which use Surrey's standard oversubscription criteria. Demand at both schools means that distance tiebreakers can be decisive; parents living north of the A3100 should check which school's catchment boundary their address falls within.

Epsom has 29 schools — 19 primaries and 4 secondaries — with admissions co-ordinated by Surrey County Council. Nineteen of the 29 schools operate as academies, and 5 carry a faith designation (Roman Catholic and Church of England), so parents should check each school's published admissions policy individually.

Epsom's secondary schools, including Blenheim High School and Rosebery School, allocate oversubscription places primarily by distance. The area is highly sought-after and some popular primaries have seen their last-offered distance fall below 0.6 km — checking the previous year's admissions data before applying is strongly advised.

Esher has 8 schools including 4 primaries and 2 secondaries, with Surrey County Council co-ordinating admissions. The area has a mix of community schools, Church of England schools and academies, each applying its own oversubscription criteria.

Demand for places at Esher's two secondary schools is high. Esher Church of England High School prioritises practising Church of England families, while Hinchley Wood School allocates on distance. Parents living near the boundary between the two catchments should verify their closest school before submitting a preference.

Fareham has 40 schools including 27 primaries and 5 secondaries, with catchment boundaries set by Hampshire County Council. The borough has grown significantly with new housing in Whiteley and Welborne, which has added pressure to several primary school catchments in recent years.

Hampshire's secondary admissions use a traditional catchment area model for community schools: pupils living within the designated catchment have priority after siblings and EHC-plan children. For secondary schools in Fareham, published catchment maps are updated every autumn in Hampshire's 'Apply for a School Place' guide.

Hyde has 22 schools including 16 primaries and 3 secondaries, administered by Tameside Metropolitan Borough Council. Nineteen schools operate as academies — one of the highest academy proportions among Greater Manchester towns — so parents need to consult each school's admissions policy alongside the council's co-ordinated scheme.

Oversubscription at Hyde's community schools is resolved by distance from home to school gate. Roman Catholic and Church of England schools in the area use faith-criteria alongside distance, and typically require evidence of regular worship from the relevant parish or diocese.

Malvern has 22 schools including 14 primaries and 2 secondaries, with admissions overseen by Herefordshire Council. Eleven schools are academies and 11 carry a faith designation (predominantly Church of England and Roman Catholic), giving Malvern one of the more complex admissions mixes for a mid-sized market town.

The main secondary schools serving Malvern are Dyson Perrins C of E Academy and The Chase Technology College. Dyson Perrins gives priority to Church of England worshippers before distance, while The Chase uses straight-line distance as its primary tiebreaker. Parents should check the published catchment maps annually as boundary shifts can affect eligibility.

Okehampton has 12 schools including 10 primaries and 1 secondary — Okehampton College — with admissions co-ordinated by Devon County Council. Nine of the twelve schools operate as academies, largely reflecting the national academy conversion trend in Devon's rural areas.

The primary schools around Okehampton typically serve clearly defined village catchments, meaning most children attend their nearest school without needing to apply through the oversubscription process. Okehampton College, as the sole secondary, admits all children from its defined catchment area before considering distance for out-of-catchment applicants.

Olney has 3 primary schools with admissions co-ordinated by Milton Keynes Council. All three schools operate as academies. There are no secondary schools within Olney itself; the nearest are in Newport Pagnell and Milton Keynes city, served by Milton Keynes's secondary transfer process.

Primary places in Olney are competitive during years of high birth cohorts. Milton Keynes Council uses straight-line distance as the tiebreaker for community academies in the town. Parents planning ahead should note that feeder school links to Newport Pagnell's secondary schools may give priority to Year 6 children at Olney primary academies.

london.seoTitle: London School Catchment Map 2026 — 994 Primaries by Postcode
london.seoDescription: London area catchment finder: 994 primary + 247 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Boroughs set their own 2026 admissions criteria — compare Ofsted ratings and last-distance-offered across Inner and Outer London.
paragraphs: London has over 1,800 schools spread across 32 boroughs and the City of London, making it by far the largest and most complex admissions landscape in England. Each borough operates as its own local authority — so catchment boundaries, oversubscription criteria and distances offered vary sharply between, for example, Barnet in the north and Southwark in the south.

In heavily oversubscribed Inner London areas, the last distance offered at popular primary schools can fall below 500 metres; in Outer London boroughs such as Bromley or Havering, distances of 1–2 km are more common. Faith schools — Church of England, Roman Catholic and Jewish — make up a significant proportion of popular schools and may draw pupils from across borough boundaries.

To search catchment areas for a specific London borough, use the council pages on catchment.school or enter your postcode in the search tool. Always cross-check with the individual school's 2026 admissions policy, as academies set their own criteria independently of the borough.

birmingham.seoTitle: Birmingham School Catchment Map 2026 — 301 Primaries by Postcode
birmingham.seoDescription: Birmingham area catchment finder: 301 primary + 85 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Birmingham City Council 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Birmingham has 517 schools, including 301 primaries and 85 secondaries, coordinated primarily by Birmingham City Council — the largest local authority by population in England. The city's admissions system covers a mix of community schools (using council-set criteria), academies, and a substantial number of faith schools representing Church of England, Roman Catholic, Islamic and other denominations.

Catchment distances at popular Birmingham primaries in areas such as Moseley, Harborne and Sutton Coldfield can be tight, often under 800 metres for the nearest-school tiebreaker. Selective grammar schools in the wider West Midlands area add a further layer to secondary school planning for some families.

Birmingham's admissions round opens each September for the following academic year. Families are advised to list all preferences carefully and to check whether faith school criteria apply, as around a third of Birmingham's schools are faith-designated.

manchester.seoTitle: Manchester School Catchment Map 2026 — 285 Primaries by Postcode
manchester.seoDescription: Manchester area catchment finder: 285 primary + 61 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Manchester, Salford and Trafford 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: The greater Manchester area has around 414 schools in the catchment.school database, spanning Manchester City Council (202 schools), Salford (60), Trafford (43) and other neighbouring authorities. Admissions criteria differ between councils, so a school just across the boundary into Salford or Trafford may use different tiebreakers than a Manchester City school on the same street.

Manchester City Council coordinates admissions for its community and voluntary-controlled schools. Many popular primaries in areas such as Didsbury, Chorlton and Fallowfield are heavily oversubscribed, with last-distance-offered sometimes falling below 600 metres. The city also has a large number of academy schools that set their own admissions policies.

The Greater Manchester Combined Authority does not coordinate school admissions; families must apply through whichever local authority the school is physically located in. Check the relevant council page on catchment.school to see the right authority for your target school.

bristol.seoTitle: Bristol School Catchment Map 2026 — 219 Primaries by Postcode
bristol.seoDescription: Bristol area catchment finder: 219 primary + 42 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Bristol City, South Gloucestershire and North Somerset 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Bristol and its surrounding areas have 320 schools in the catchment.school database, split across Bristol City Council (164 schools), South Gloucestershire (106) and North Somerset (27). Families living near the council boundaries in areas such as Filton, Kingswood or Nailsea should pay close attention to which authority a school falls under, as admissions criteria differ.

Within Bristol City, popular primaries in areas such as Redland, Clifton and Stoke Bishop are consistently oversubscribed, with distance tiebreakers sometimes falling below 700 metres. Bristol operates a Fair Banding system for some secondary schools to ensure a broad intake, which changes how secondary admissions work compared to purely distance-based systems.

Bristol's coordinated admissions round runs from September; secondary applications typically close in October for Year 7 entry. Check Bristol City Council's published admissions policy alongside each school's own prospectus, particularly for academy and faith schools.

nottingham.seoTitle: Nottingham School Catchment Map 2026 — 225 Primaries by Postcode
nottingham.seoDescription: Nottingham area catchment finder: 225 primary + 42 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Nottingham City, Nottinghamshire and Derbyshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: The Nottingham area spans 307 schools across Nottingham City Council (114 schools), Nottinghamshire County (166) and parts of Derbyshire (24). The city boundary is a key dividing line: schools in West Bridgford, Arnold or Carlton sit in Nottinghamshire, not Nottingham City — each with their own admissions criteria.

Nottingham City coordinates admissions for community schools within the city boundary. Some popular primaries in areas such as Wollaton, Mapperley and West Bridgford attract applications from a wide catchment, with distance tiebreakers of under a mile at the most sought-after schools. Cheshire East Council coordinates admissions for community schools, applying a nearest-school preference as the main tiebreaker.

Sandbach's two secondary schools — Sandbach School (boys) and Sandbach High School and Sixth Form College (mixed) — serve the town and surrounding villages including Elworth and Holmes Chapel. Sandbach School is a selective boys' grammar school that admits via the Cheshire East grammar entrance test, so families considering secondary options should check the selective criteria separately.

stevenage.seoTitle: Stevenage School Catchment Map 2026 — 42 Schools by Postcode
stevenage.seoDescription: Stevenage area catchment finder: 42 schools (29 primary, 6 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Hertfordshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Stevenage was the UK's first designated new town and retains a neighbourhood structure with 42 state schools — 29 primaries and 6 secondaries — organised around the town's residential zones. Hertfordshire County Council coordinates admissions and links primary schools to secondary feeders that reflect the original new-town planning.

Six secondary schools serve Stevenage, and Hertfordshire applies feeder-school preferences at most of them. Families who move into the area partway through primary school may not attend a feeder school and so fall back on a distance tiebreaker for secondary allocation — checking the current feeder-link list via Hertfordshire's admissions portal is strongly advised.

sudbury.seoTitle: Sudbury School Catchment Map 2026 — 24 Schools by Postcode
sudbury.seoDescription: Sudbury area catchment finder: 24 schools (17 primary, 3 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Essex admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Sudbury is a market town on the River Stour at the Suffolk–Essex border with 24 state schools, including 17 primaries serving the town and a wide cluster of surrounding villages. Essex County Council coordinates admissions for community schools in the Essex portion of the catchment, while Suffolk County Council administers schools on the Suffolk side.

Because the area straddles two local authority boundaries, families near Great Cornard or Acton should check which council administers their nearest schools before applying. Sudbury's three secondary schools serve an extensive rural catchment — competition for Year 7 places at the most popular schools can be significant for families more than 3 miles from their preferred school.

watford.seoTitle: Watford School Catchment Map 2026 — 52 Schools by Postcode
watford.seoDescription: Watford area catchment finder: 52 schools (36 primary, 6 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Hertfordshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Watford is a commercial town on the edge of Greater London in Hertfordshire with 52 state schools — 36 primaries and 6 secondaries — serving a densely populated area that includes Bushey, Garston and Leavesden. Hertfordshire County Council coordinates admissions, and the town's compact geography means several primary schools are consistently oversubscribed.

Watford's proximity to London attracts families pricing out of the capital, keeping demand for the most popular primaries high. Several of Watford's secondaries have been graded Outstanding by Ofsted, increasing competition at Year 7. Families should note that some Hertfordshire secondaries use feeder-school preferences, so the primary school chosen may affect secondary allocation.

winchester.seoTitle: Winchester School Catchment Map 2026 — 35 Schools by Postcode
winchester.seoDescription: Winchester area catchment finder: 35 schools (21 primary, 2 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Hampshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Winchester is Hampshire's historic cathedral city and county town, with 35 state schools including 21 primaries serving the city and a broad rural catchment across mid-Hampshire villages such as Itchen Abbas and Kings Worthy. Hampshire County Council coordinates admissions and publishes annual catchment boundaries.

Winchester has only two state secondary schools — Henry Beaufort and Kings' School — for the city's catchment, which creates significant competition at Year 7. Hampshire's secondary admissions use a nearest-school tiebreaker, and the last distance offered at Winchester's secondaries can fall well below 2 miles in competitive years; families in outlying villages should apply to both and consider Eastleigh or Romsey secondaries as alternatives.

cambridge.seoTitle: Cambridge School Catchment Areas 2026 — 127 Schools by Postcode
cambridge.seoDescription: Cambridge area catchment finder: 78 primary + 16 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Cambridgeshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Cambridge has 127 schools across the city and its surrounding villages, administered by Cambridgeshire County Council. The city's mix of community schools, Church of England primaries, and selective grammar schools means admissions criteria vary significantly — some schools prioritise faith, others use strict distance tiebreakers. Popular schools in central Cambridge have historically offered places to children living within 0.5 miles, so checking the latest 'last distance offered' data before applying is essential.

Secondary admissions in Cambridge are particularly competitive. Hills Road Sixth Form College and Chesterton Community College draw applications from across the county, while selective schools require the Cambridgeshire 11+ test. For primary applications, the council's coordinated scheme deadline is typically mid-January for September entry — catchment boundaries are reviewed annually and can shift year to year.

milton-keynes.seoTitle: Milton Keynes School Catchment Areas 2026 — 119 Schools by Postcode
milton-keynes.seoDescription: Milton Keynes area catchment finder: 85 primary + 12 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Milton Keynes has 119 schools across the borough, including 85 primary and 12 secondary schools. As a planned city with distinct housing areas — from Wolverton and Newport Pagnell to the modern grid squares of central MK — catchment boundaries often align with neighbourhood boundaries. Milton Keynes Council coordinates admissions, with most community schools using distance as the main tiebreaker after looked-after children and siblings.

Secondary schools in Milton Keynes include a mix of academies, free schools, and community comprehensives. Stantonbury School and Denbigh School are among the most established, drawing pupils from across the borough. For families in newer developments such as Tattenhoe or Kingsmead, it is worth checking the designated catchment school carefully, as boundaries are updated each year to reflect new housing.

hull.seoTitle: Hull School Catchment Areas 2026 — 117 Schools by Postcode
hull.seoDescription: Hull (Kingston upon Hull) catchment finder: 87 primary + 14 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered.
paragraphs: Hull (Kingston upon Hull) has 117 schools across the city, with 87 primary and 14 secondary schools administered by Hull City Council. The city is structured into distinct neighbourhoods — from Bransholme and Anlaby Road in the north and west to Holderness Road and Longhill in the east — and catchment areas broadly follow these geographic divides. Most community schools use proximity as the key tiebreaker after siblings.

Secondary education in Hull includes a number of high-performing academies. Sirius Academy West and Malet Lambert are among the most sought-after, with demand sometimes exceeding catchment distances of under one mile. Hull has invested significantly in school improvement, and Ofsted judgements across the city have improved markedly since 2019. Families should apply through the council's coordinated scheme by mid-January for September secondary places.

oldham.seoTitle: Oldham School Catchment Areas 2026 — 114 Schools by Postcode
oldham.seoDescription: Oldham area catchment finder: 79 primary + 13 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Oldham has 114 schools across the metropolitan borough, including 79 primary and 13 secondary schools. Oldham Council coordinates admissions for community and voluntary-controlled schools, while academies and voluntary-aided schools manage their own admissions within the same national framework. The borough spans a wide area — from the town centre to outlying settlements like Saddleworth, Shaw, and Lees — and catchment distances reflect population density.

Secondary schools in Oldham include Royton and Crompton Academy and Oldham Academy North among those with strong recent Ofsted judgements. The borough has a high proportion of faith schools at both primary and secondary level, several of which admit pupils from across the borough based on religious criteria rather than proximity. Families should review each school's individual admissions policy alongside the council's composite prospectus when making applications.

stockport.seoTitle: Stockport School Catchment Areas 2026 — 113 Schools by Postcode
stockport.seoDescription: Stockport catchment finder: 76 primary + 11 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Stockport has 113 schools across the metropolitan borough, administered by Stockport Council. The borough stretches from Hazel Grove and Bramhall in the south to Reddish and Heaton Chapel bordering Manchester in the north — and school catchment areas tend to be tighter in more densely populated areas like Edgeley, where primary places are heavily contested. Distance tiebreakers for popular Stockport primaries can be as little as 0.3 miles in some years.

At secondary level, Stockport has a selective grammar school — Stockport Grammar School — alongside a range of academies and community schools. The grammar schools admit by 11+ test and draw from across the borough and neighbouring areas, so non-selective catchment distances for comprehensives can be wider. Schools in sought-after postcodes such as SK7 (Bramhall/Cheadle Hulme) are often oversubscribed, and families should check annual offer data carefully before choosing a home.

plymouth.seoTitle: Plymouth School Catchment Areas 2026 — 113 Schools by Postcode
plymouth.seoDescription: Plymouth catchment finder: 76 primary + 19 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Plymouth has 113 schools across the city, including 76 primary and 19 secondary schools, administered by Plymouth City Council. The city is divided into distinct communities — Devonport, Plymstock, Plympton, Peverell, and St Jude's among them — and catchment areas broadly reflect these neighbourhoods. Most community schools use proximity as the primary tiebreaker, with popular primaries in central and east Plymouth historically offering places within 0.6 miles.

Secondary education in Plymouth includes a strong set of academies. Plymouth School of Creative Arts is a specialist arts academy that attracts applications from across the city, while Devonport High School for Boys and Devonport High School for Girls are selective grammar schools admitting via the Devon 11+ test. The council's coordinated scheme deadline for secondary applications is the national closing date of 31 October each year.

lincoln.seoTitle: Lincoln School Catchment Areas 2026 — 108 Schools by Postcode
lincoln.seoDescription: Lincoln catchment finder: 76 primary + 13 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Lincolnshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Lincoln and its surrounding area has 108 schools, with 76 primary and 13 secondary schools co-ordinated by Lincolnshire County Council. The city has grown rapidly on its southern and western edges, with new housing estates in Birchwood, North Hykeham, and Skellingthorpe increasing pressure on local schools. Catchment boundaries in these growth areas are reviewed annually, and families in newer developments should verify their designated school early.

Secondary education in Lincoln includes both selective and non-selective options. The City of Lincoln Academy and Lincoln UTC are popular non-selective choices, while the county's grammar schools — including Lincoln Minster School and Christ's Hospital School — admit on selective criteria. For families seeking grammar school places, registration deadlines and 11+ test dates fall in the summer term of Year 5, well ahead of the standard admissions timeline.

walsall.seoTitle: Walsall School Catchment Areas 2026 — 107 Schools by Postcode
walsall.seoDescription: Walsall catchment finder: 69 primary + 15 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Walsall has 107 schools across the metropolitan borough, with 69 primary and 15 secondary schools. Walsall Council coordinates admissions for community and voluntary-controlled schools, but the borough has a significant proportion of academies that set their own admissions criteria. Areas such as Streetly, Aldridge, and Brownhills tend to have more oversubscribed schools than the town centre, and popular primaries in these areas have historically offered places within 0.4 miles.

At secondary level, Queen Mary's Grammar School in Walsall town centre is one of the West Midlands' highest-achieving selective schools, drawing applicants from across the borough and beyond via the NFER 11+ test. Non-selective secondary schools in the borough include several outstanding academies. Families should note that Walsall sits within the West Midlands grammar school area, meaning selective places are available without needing to live within a specific catchment boundary.

swindon.seoTitle: Swindon School Catchment Areas 2026 — 106 Schools by Postcode
swindon.seoDescription: Swindon catchment finder: 77 primary + 15 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Swindon has 106 schools across the borough, with 77 primary and 15 secondary schools administered by Swindon Borough Council. The town has expanded rapidly westward into the Wichelstowe and Tadpole Garden Village developments, creating additional pressure on existing schools and prompting new free schools to open. Families buying in newer estates should confirm which school they are linked to — designated catchment schools for new builds are not always the nearest geographically.

Secondary schools in Swindon include Churchfields Academy, Ridgeway School, and Nova Hreod Academy, with Cirencester's selective Deer Park school accessible to some border postcodes. Swindon Borough Council publishes its composite prospectus each autumn with admissions policies for every school, and the national secondary deadline of 31 October applies. Primary school applications close in mid-January for September entry.

bedford.seoTitle: Bedford School Catchment Areas 2026 — 103 Schools by Postcode
bedford.seoDescription: Bedford catchment finder: 66 primary + 14 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Bedford has 103 schools across the borough, with 66 primary and 14 secondary schools. Bedford Borough Council coordinates admissions for community schools, while the borough's significant proportion of voluntary-aided and academy schools manage their own criteria. Bedford town has a diverse population — including a large Italian-heritage community in Kempston — and school popularity varies considerably across the borough's neighbourhoods.

Bedford is unusual in retaining upper schools in a three-tier system across parts of the borough, with pupils moving from first school to middle school at Year 5, then to upper school at Year 9. Families new to the area should check carefully whether their postcode falls within the two-tier or three-tier catchment structure. The borough's selective upper school, Bedford Academy, admits via entrance test and draws from across the borough.

warrington.seoTitle: Warrington School Catchment Areas 2026 — 102 Schools by Postcode
warrington.seoDescription: Warrington catchment finder: 77 primary + 14 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Warrington has 102 schools across the borough, with 77 primary and 14 secondary schools administered by Warrington Borough Council. Situated between Manchester and Liverpool, Warrington has grown significantly through planned housing developments in Chapelford, Omega, and South Warrington, increasing demand for local school places. Catchment areas in newer housing zones are carefully monitored and updated annually.

Secondary schools in Warrington include Bridgewater High School, The Grange School, and Cardinal Newman Catholic High School, among others. The borough has a strong Catholic school tradition, with several voluntary-aided primaries and secondaries that admit on faith criteria independently of the council's catchment areas. Families applying for faith school places should contact individual schools directly to understand their supplementary information form requirements.

wigan.seoTitle: Wigan School Catchment Areas 2026 — 101 Schools by Postcode
wigan.seoDescription: Wigan catchment finder: 70 primary + 13 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Wigan metropolitan borough has 101 schools, with 70 primary and 13 secondary schools across towns including Wigan, Leigh, Atherton, and Hindley. Wigan Council coordinates admissions for community and voluntary-controlled schools; most use proximity as the primary tiebreaker after looked-after children and siblings. Catchment areas in Leigh and the eastern townships tend to be larger than in Wigan town centre due to lower population density.

Secondary education in Wigan includes a number of high-performing academies and faith schools. Wigan and Leigh College is a significant post-16 provider drawing from across the borough. Several Catholic secondary schools in the borough admit on faith criteria via the council's coordinated scheme but use their own supplementary information forms. Families should check each school's published admissions policy in the council's composite prospectus, available each autumn.

rotherham.seoTitle: Rotherham School Catchment Areas 2026 — 101 Schools by Postcode
rotherham.seoDescription: Rotherham catchment finder: 76 primary + 13 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Rotherham metropolitan borough has 101 schools, with 76 primary and 13 secondary schools administered by Rotherham Council. The borough spans from the town centre through to Maltby, Dinnington, and the rural parishes of Rother Valley. School improvement has been a significant focus following the council's improvement journey since 2015, and Ofsted judgements across Rotherham's schools have improved substantially in recent years.

Secondary schools in Rotherham include Oakwood High School, Wales High School, and Aston Academy. The borough also has a number of faith schools that use religious criteria for oversubscription. For families relocating to the area, Rotherham's composite prospectus is published each October and includes detailed catchment maps, admissions criteria, and historical 'last distance offered' data for every school in the borough.

ipswich.seoTitle: Ipswich School Catchment Areas 2026 — 98 Schools by Postcode
ipswich.seoDescription: Ipswich catchment finder: 62 primary + 12 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Suffolk admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Ipswich has 98 schools across the town and its surrounding parishes, with 62 primary and 12 secondary schools. Suffolk County Council coordinates admissions for community schools, while the town's academies and faith schools manage their own criteria. Ipswich is Suffolk's county town and largest urban area, with popular primaries in the Rushmere, Whitton, and Clapgate areas historically offering places within 0.5 miles in oversubscribed years.

Secondary education in Ipswich includes Northgate High School, Ormiston Endeavour Academy, and Suffolk New College for post-16 study. Several of Ipswich's secondary schools have been converted to academy status in recent years, meaning they hold their own admissions authority. Suffolk County Council publishes annual admissions data including each school's published admission number and last distance offered — essential reading for families choosing secondary schools.

oxford.seoTitle: Oxford School Catchment Areas 2026 — 95 Schools by Postcode
oxford.seoDescription: Oxford catchment finder: 48 primary + 8 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Oxfordshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Oxford has 95 schools across the city, with 48 primary and 8 secondary schools. Oxfordshire County Council coordinates admissions for the city's community schools, though many of Oxford's primaries are Church of England voluntary-aided schools that manage their own admissions. The city is split into catchment areas roughly along the axes of the Cowley Road, Headington, Jericho, and Summertown neighbourhoods, with popular schools in north and east Oxford historically receiving more applications than places.

Oxford's eight secondary schools are all non-selective comprehensives — the county retains no grammar schools. Cherwell School, Oxford Spires Academy, and Cheney School are among the most in-demand, with popular schools sometimes offering places to children living within 1 mile. Oxford's large transient academic population (associated with the university) means school rolls can fluctuate; the council's annual admissions data is the most reliable guide to current catchment distances.

middlesbrough.seoTitle: Middlesbrough School Catchment Areas 2026 — 89 Schools by Postcode
middlesbrough.seoDescription: Middlesbrough catchment finder: 61 primary + 11 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Middlesbrough has 89 schools, with 61 primary and 11 secondary schools administered by Middlesbrough Council. The borough covers the town centre and outer suburbs including Marton, Acklam, and Hemlington. School admissions in Middlesbrough are coordinated by the council, with most community schools using proximity as the primary tiebreaker. Catchment areas in more affluent southern suburbs such as Marton tend to be tighter due to higher demand.

Secondary schools in Middlesbrough include Outwood Academy Acklam, Macmillan Academy, and Unity City Academy. The area has seen significant academy conversion since 2010, meaning most secondary schools set their own admissions criteria within the national framework. Middlesbrough is adjacent to Redcar & Cleveland and Stockton-on-Tees, so families close to borough boundaries may wish to consider cross-boundary applications — the council's coordinated scheme accommodates preferences outside Middlesbrough.

gwynedd.seoTitle: Gwynedd School Catchment Areas 2026 — 89 Schools by Postcode
gwynedd.seoDescription: Gwynedd catchment finder: 89 schools across North Wales mapped to your postcode. Welsh-medium and English-medium admissions criteria, Ofsted/Estyn ratings for 2026.
paragraphs: Gwynedd has 89 schools across a large, predominantly rural county in north-west Wales, administered by Gwynedd Council. As a stronghold of the Welsh language, the vast majority of Gwynedd's schools are Welsh-medium — meaning lessons are conducted in Welsh, with English taught as a second language. Families relocating to the county from England or non-Welsh-speaking areas should be aware that their nearest school may well be Welsh-medium, and that English-medium provision in some parts of the county is limited.

School catchment areas in Gwynedd tend to be geographically large, reflecting low population density across Snowdonia and the Llŷn Peninsula. Bangor and Caernarfon are the largest urban centres with the greatest choice of schools. Gwynedd Council's admissions authority is Cyngor Gwynedd, and schools in the county are inspected by Estyn (the Wales education inspectorate) rather than Ofsted. Families should consult both Cyngor Gwynedd's admissions policies and Estyn inspection reports when choosing schools.

swansea.seoTitle: Swansea School Catchment Areas 2026 — 89 Schools by Postcode
swansea.seoDescription: Swansea catchment finder: 89 schools across the city mapped to your postcode. Welsh-medium and English-medium admissions criteria, Estyn ratings for 2026.
paragraphs: Swansea (Abertawe) has 89 schools across the city and its surrounding areas, administered by City and County of Swansea Council. The city offers a mix of Welsh-medium and English-medium schools at both primary and secondary level, making it one of the key centres for Welsh-language education in south Wales. Popular English-medium primaries in Sketty, Uplands, and the city centre tend to be oversubscribed, with proximity and siblings as the main tiebreakers.

Secondary schools in Swansea include Olchfa School, Bishop Gore School, and Gowerton School, the latter serving the Gower Peninsula. The bilingual Welsh medium secondary, Ysgol Gymraeg Bryn Tawe, draws pupils from across the city. Schools in Swansea are inspected by Estyn, and the council's composite prospectus is published each autumn. Families considering Welsh-medium education should note that demand for Welsh-medium places has grown significantly in recent years, and waiting lists can develop even mid-year.

huddersfield.seoTitle: Huddersfield School Catchment Areas 2026 — 88 Schools by Postcode
huddersfield.seoDescription: Huddersfield catchment finder: 63 primary + 9 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Kirklees admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Huddersfield has 88 schools across the town and surrounding townships, with 63 primary and 9 secondary schools administered by Kirklees Council. The borough of Kirklees is one of England's largest metropolitan boroughs, and Huddersfield is its main town. Catchment areas in Huddersfield tend to reflect the town's distinct communities — Lindley, Marsh, Moldgreen, and Lockwood — with popular primaries in western Huddersfield historically offering places within 0.5 miles.

Secondary schools in Huddersfield include Almondbury Community School, Newsome Academy, and North Huddersfield Trust School. The area has a high proportion of academy schools at secondary level. Kirklees Council coordinates admissions and publishes detailed catchment data annually. Families considering grammar school education should note that the West Riding Grammar School in Heckmondwike serves much of Kirklees, with selective places available via the 11+ test to children from across the borough.

gloucester.seoTitle: Gloucester School Catchment Areas 2026 — 88 Schools by Postcode
gloucester.seoDescription: Gloucester catchment finder: 64 primary + 12 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Gloucestershire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Gloucester has 88 schools across the city and its surrounding parishes, with 64 primary and 12 secondary schools administered by Gloucestershire County Council. The city has seen significant housing growth in Quedgeley, Kingsway, and Innsworth, increasing pressure on popular primary schools. Catchment areas in these growth zones are reviewed annually, and families in new housing developments should confirm their linked school before applying.

Secondary education in Gloucester is non-selective — Gloucestershire retains no grammar schools within the city boundary, though grammar schools in Cheltenham are accessible to some Gloucester postcodes. The Barnwood Park School, Sir Thomas Rich's School (in nearby Longlevens), and Denmark Road High School are among the most sought-after secondaries. Sir Thomas Rich's is a selective school admitting via the Gloucestershire Grammar School test. All secondary applications go through the council's coordinated scheme, with the national deadline of 31 October applying.

barry.seoTitle: Barry School Catchment Map 2026 — Vale of Glamorgan Schools by Postcode
barry.seoDescription: Barry area catchment finder: 13 schools mapped to your postcode. Vale of Glamorgan 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted and Welsh-medium options — free.
paragraphs: Barry is the Vale of Glamorgan's largest town, with 13 schools administered by Vale of Glamorgan Council. Like Cardiff, the Vale operates parallel Welsh-medium and English-medium streams, and Barry has dedicated Welsh-medium provision at both primary and secondary level — Ysgol Gymraeg Barry is the main Welsh-medium primary, while Ysgol Bro Morgannwg secondary serves Welsh-medium learners across the Vale.

English-medium secondaries in Barry include Barry Comprehensive School and Stanwell School. The Vale publishes its catchment maps and co-ordinated admissions timetable each September; applications are managed through the council's admissions portal. Welsh-medium catchments are typically borough-wide rather than defined by close proximity.

loughton.seoTitle: Loughton School Catchment Map 2026 — Essex Schools by Postcode
loughton.seoDescription: Loughton area catchment finder: 14 schools mapped to your postcode. Essex 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year — free.
paragraphs: Loughton sits in the Epping Forest district of Essex, with 14 schools split between 8 primaries and 3 secondaries. Essex County Council co-ordinates maintained school admissions here, and proximity to the Tube's Central line makes this one of the more commuter-oriented corners of Essex — with school oversubscription tracking closely with housing demand.

Davenant Foundation School and Roding Valley High School are the main secondary options, both well-regarded and drawing from a catchment that spans Loughton, Buckhurst Hill and the Debden area. Essex sets secondary preferences by the 31 October deadline and primary preferences by mid-January; late applications move to the bottom of the allocation order.

ware.seoTitle: Ware School Catchment Map 2026 — 16 Primary & 2 Secondary Schools
ware.seoDescription: Ware area catchment finder: 24 schools mapped to your postcode. Hertfordshire 2026 admissions, Ofsted ratings and distance offered at last allocation round — free.
paragraphs: Ware is a Hertfordshire market town on the River Lea with 24 schools — 16 primaries and 2 secondaries. Hertfordshire County Council co-ordinates admissions, using its home-to-school distance algorithm for community schools. Ware's growth as a commuter settlement has tightened primary competition in some zones, particularly along the A10 corridor.

The two main secondaries — Presdales (girls, partially selective) and Ware Academy — serve different catchments. Presdales operates a partially-selective entry for girls showing high ability and draws applicants from well beyond Ware itself; Ware Academy is fully comprehensive and caters primarily to the town and immediate villages. Hertfordshire's co-ordinated secondary timetable requires preferences by the October deadline.

luton.seoTitle: Luton School Catchment Areas 2026 — 52 Primary & 14 Secondary | Luton
luton.seoDescription: Luton catchment finder: 84 schools — 52 primary + 14 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Luton Borough 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last-distance-offered data — free.
paragraphs: Luton has 84 schools including 52 primaries and 14 secondaries, all administered by Luton Borough Council as the local admissions authority. A unitary authority since 1997, Luton runs a single annual admissions round with most community schools oversubscribed in central and east Luton postcodes — areas such as Bury Park and Farley Hill regularly fill on straight-line distance.

Secondary demand is particularly competitive around Luton's Sixth Form College feeder schools. A significant proportion of Luton secondaries are academies, each setting their own admissions criteria, so families should check individual school policies alongside the council's co-ordinated offer. The council publishes its secondary determined arrangements each September for the following September's intake.

exeter.seoTitle: Exeter School Catchment Areas 2026 — 53 Primary & 6 Secondary | Devon
exeter.seoDescription: Exeter catchment finder: 84 Devon schools — 53 primary + 6 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year — free.
paragraphs: Exeter has 84 schools including 53 primaries and 6 secondary schools, coordinated by Devon County Council. Exeter is Devon's county city and a fast-growing university city — new residential developments in Cranbrook and Pinhoe have driven steady demand for primary places, with several schools in the city centre regularly oversubscribed in the first two or three kilometre bands.

Secondary provision in Exeter includes a mix of community, faith and academy schools. Exeter School (independent) dominates fee-paying education, but the state secondary sector covers the city well. Devon coordinates all state secondary admissions; families in newer estates should check catchment maps carefully as boundaries have shifted with new school openings in recent years.

chelmsford.seoTitle: Chelmsford School Catchment Areas 2026 — 56 Primary & 10 Secondary | Essex
chelmsford.seoDescription: Chelmsford catchment finder: 84 Essex schools — 56 primary + 10 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year — free.
paragraphs: Chelmsford has 84 schools including 56 primaries and 10 secondaries, coordinated by Essex County Council. As Essex's county city, Chelmsford attracts strong commuter demand, and primary catchments in Springfield, Moulsham and Broomfield routinely fill within 800 metres of the school gate. Essex operates a published admissions scheme, but the 44 academy and voluntary-aided schools in the area each set additional criteria.

Secondary competition in Chelmsford includes some of the highest demand in Essex — KEGS (King Edward VI Grammar School) and Chelmsford County High for Girls are selective and draw from across the county, while non-selective secondaries often fill on distance. Families new to the area should check whether their address falls within a school's priority zone before relying on the council's coordinated scheme.

chesterfield.seoTitle: Chesterfield School Catchment Areas 2026 — 63 Primary & 11 Secondary | Derbyshire
chesterfield.seoDescription: Chesterfield catchment finder: 83 Derbyshire schools — 63 primary + 11 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last-offered data — free.
paragraphs: Chesterfield has 83 schools including 63 primaries and 11 secondaries, administered by Derbyshire County Council. The market town's dense school network means most families live within a kilometre of at least two primary schools, but popular schools in Hasland, Walton and the town centre regularly fill on distance in years of above-average applications.

Secondary demand in Chesterfield is driven by a mix of academy and community schools. Derbyshire has no grammar schools, so secondary allocation is fully comprehensive and managed through Derbyshire's coordinated scheme. Chesterfield's ongoing new housing development in the eastern parishes has periodically triggered admission number reviews at the nearest schools.

barnsley.seoTitle: Barnsley School Catchment Areas 2026 — 64 Primary & 8 Secondary | Barnsley
