gillingham.seoTitle: Schools in Gillingham Dorset Catchment Area 2026 — Map & Admissions Guide
gillingham.seoDescription: Gillingham (Dorset) catchment area: 43 schools across the north Dorset market town and surrounding villages. Admissions criteria, catchment maps and 2026 guide.
paragraphs: Gillingham is a small market town in the Blackmore Vale, and its 43 schools cover a broad rural area across north Dorset — taking in Shaftesbury, Mere, Sturminster Newton, Stalbridge and the surrounding villages. Dorset Council coordinates all maintained school admissions in this area and publishes catchment boundary maps annually.

Gillingham School is the main secondary for the town, drawing from a large rural catchment. Oversubscription resolves on distance; families in the outer villages should check whether their address falls within the defined catchment or would be treated as an out-of-catchment application.

Many primaries in this part of Dorset are small village schools with single or mixed-age classes. Capacity is limited and catchments are drawn tightly around each village, so families in rural hamlets between two settlements should confirm which school their postcode designates them for.

newark.seoTitle: Schools in Newark Catchment Area 2026 — Map & Admissions Guide
newark.seoDescription: Newark catchment area: 43 schools across Newark-on-Trent and surrounding Nottinghamshire villages. Admissions criteria, catchment maps and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Newark-on-Trent's 43 schools serve the historic Nottinghamshire market town and a spread of Trent Valley villages — Southwell, Balderton, Collingham, East Markham and many smaller parishes. Nottinghamshire County Council coordinates all maintained school admissions, publishing catchment maps and oversubscription criteria each autumn.

Secondary school provision in Newark runs through the Magnus Academy, the Minster School, Lilac Grove Academy and Dukeries Academy. All operate individual admissions policies; families should check each school's specific criteria as they differ from each other and from the Nottinghamshire default.

Village primaries around Newark are typically small and heavily oversubscribed by local residents, leaving little space for out-of-catchment applicants. Using the school's published last-offered distance from prior years will give the most reliable sense of whether an address realistically qualifies.

dagenham.seoTitle: Schools in Dagenham Catchment Area 2026 — Map & Admissions Guide
dagenham.seoDescription: Dagenham catchment area: 42 schools across the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham. Admissions criteria, catchment boundaries and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Dagenham forms the eastern half of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham and its 42 schools reflect the borough's dense residential character — primarily primary schools serving each housing estate, from Becontree in the west to Marks Gate in the east. The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham acts as the admissions authority for community schools and coordinates pan-London secondary applications.

Primary school catchments in Dagenham are small: with many schools sitting close together across the Becontree estate, the last-admitted distance at popular schools can be as little as a few hundred metres. Siblings and looked-after children take precedence, then straightforward home-to-school distance.

Secondary school choices open up beyond Dagenham itself through the pan-London application process, but schools in the immediate area include Robert Clack School (outstanding), Jo Richardson Community School and Sydney Russell. Application data from the borough shows most secondary pupils attend schools within or immediately adjacent to Dagenham.

harlow.seoTitle: Schools in Harlow Catchment Area 2026 — Map & Admissions Guide
harlow.seoDescription: Harlow catchment area: 42 schools across Essex new town neighbourhoods and surrounding villages. Catchment maps, admissions criteria and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Harlow is a post-war Essex new town whose 42 schools are spread across its residential neighbourhoods — Staple Tye, Netteswell, Latton, Church Langley, Potter Street and the older town-centre wards. Essex County Council coordinates maintained school admissions and publishes neighbourhood catchment boundaries each autumn.

Harlow's new-town design means each residential neighbourhood was planned with a primary school: many primaries are Church of England voluntary-aided schools built alongside housing estates, and faith criteria apply ahead of distance for practising Christian families. For non-faith applicants, straightforward proximity determines priority.

Secondary options in Harlow include Passmores Academy, Stewards Academy and Burnt Mill Academy. Essex's published admissions data shows last-offered distances that vary significantly between schools year on year, reflecting population movements across the borough.

woking.seoTitle: Schools in Woking Catchment Area 2026 — Map & Admissions Guide
woking.seoDescription: Woking catchment area: 42 schools across the Surrey commuter town and surrounding villages. Admissions criteria, catchment maps and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Woking is one of Surrey's main commuter towns and its 42 schools serve a mix of urban neighbourhoods — Horsell, Knaphill, Sheerwater, Pyrford and Old Woking — plus rural parishes stretching to Send, Ripley and Bisley. Surrey County Council coordinates maintained school admissions and publishes catchment maps annually.

Secondary school places in Woking are hotly contested: Winston Churchill School, Woking High School and Bishop David Brown School all have defined catchment areas, and the last-admitted distance in popular years has been as low as 0.5 miles for in-catchment applicants. Living within the published catchment is close to essential at the most popular schools.

Surrey's admissions system uses a straight-line measurement from the home address to the school entrance. Families who have recently moved should ensure their new address is registered with Surrey County Council's admissions team before the October secondary closing date.

northwich.seoTitle: Schools in Northwich Catchment Area 2026 — Map & Admissions Guide
northwich.seoDescription: Northwich catchment area: 41 schools across the Cheshire West market town and Weaver Valley villages. Admissions criteria, catchment maps and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Northwich sits in the Weaver Valley at the heart of Cheshire West and Chester, and its 41 schools span the town itself and surrounding villages including Winsford, Middlewich, Moulton, Hartford and Weaverham. Cheshire West and Chester Council coordinates all maintained school admissions, publishing catchment boundaries each autumn.

Secondary provision in Northwich runs through Hartford High School, Rudheath Academy and The Weaverham School, each with defined geographic catchments. Cheshire West operates a mixed secondary landscape with no selective schools in this area, so all places resolve on distance after looked-after children and siblings.

The salt-mining heritage of the Northwich area has left some areas of ground subsidence that have historically affected school building footprints; most schools are now on stable modern sites. School places are moderately competitive, with last-admitted distances typically in the 0.5–2 mile range depending on the school and year.

lancaster.seoTitle: Schools in Lancaster Catchment Area 2026 — Map & Admissions Guide
lancaster.seoDescription: Lancaster catchment area: 41 schools across the Lancashire city and Morecambe Bay villages. Catchment maps, admissions criteria and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Lancaster is Lancashire's county town and a university city, and its 41 schools serve the city itself plus the Morecambe Bay coastline communities of Morecambe, Heysham and the Lune Valley villages. Lancashire County Council coordinates maintained school admissions across the area and publishes catchment maps annually.

Non-selective secondaries — Ripley St Thomas, Central Lancaster High and Morecambe Bay Academy — operate defined catchment areas, with proximity as the main tiebreaker.

Lancaster's university population creates a degree of transience in the primary school estate, so place availability can vary year on year. Families should apply in the autumn before their desired September entry and confirm catchment boundaries directly with Lancashire admissions, as minor updates are published annually.

chichester.seoTitle: Schools in Chichester Catchment Area 2026 — Map & Admissions Guide
chichester.seoDescription: Chichester catchment area: 41 schools across the West Sussex cathedral city and South Downs villages. Catchment maps, admissions criteria and 2026 school guide.

keighley.seoTitle: Schools in Keighley Catchment Area 2026 — Map & Admissions Guide

Bradford has a legacy of faith-school provision across both primary and secondary phases; families should check each school's admissions criteria carefully, as CofE and Catholic schools apply faith criteria ahead of distance.

gravesend.seoTitle: Schools in Gravesend Catchment Area 2026 — Map & Admissions Guide
gravesend.seoDescription: Gravesend catchment area: 40 schools across the Kent Thames estuary town and Northfleet area. Admissions criteria, catchment maps and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Gravesend and neighbouring Northfleet sit on the south bank of the Thames estuary in north-west Kent, and their 40 schools serve a densely settled urban corridor stretching from Cobham and Meopham in the rural south to the river frontage in the north. Primary schools in Gravesend are served by a mix of community and Church of England schools. In-catchment places at community primaries resolve on distance, while CofE schools apply faith criteria first. Gravesend's housing growth means some schools operate close to or above published capacity, making early engagement with Kent admissions important.

truro.seoDescription: Truro area catchment finder: 26 primary + 3 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Cornwall Council 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.

maidenhead.seoDescription: Maidenhead area catchment finder: 24 primary + 5 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Windsor and Maidenhead 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
